name: Brinjal
perishability: Highly perishable. 3–5 days at room temperature before it wilts and loses gloss.
summary: India is the crop's home and grows thousands of local types, from long purple to the small round green Mattu Gulla. It is grown all year close to cities and moves mostly within a few hundred kilometres, so prices are regional. The shoot and fruit borer makes it one of the most heavily sprayed vegetables.

global: India is the centre of origin and diversity of brinjal and the world's second-largest producer after China. Exports are small (UAE, UK, Gulf).

seasons.name: Kharif
seasons.note: Rainy season raises pest and disease pressure.

seasons.name: Rabi
seasons.note: Best quality; winter glut keeps prices low.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.note: Heat cuts fruit set; borer peaks.

lean_season: June–September: rain and borer damage cut marketable fruit.

climate.v: Warm-season crop; 21–30 °C ideal. Stunted below ~17 °C; killed by frost.
Tolerates heat better than tomato, but fruit set drops above ~35 °C.
Deep, fertile loam, pH 5.5–6.6. Long-duration crop (5–8 months of picking).
Regular irrigation; waterlogging causes wilt and root rot.

weather_risks.impact: Fruit rot, Phomopsis blight, and borer flare-ups; fewer pickings.
Plants lodged and fields flooded in the main eastern belts.
weather_risks.example: Cyclone Amphan (May 2020) and Yaas (May 2021) in Bengal and Odisha.

weather_risks.impact: Flower drop and small, dull fruit.

pests.name: Brinjal shoot and fruit borer
pests.impact: Bores into shoots and fruit; 30–70% losses without control; drives spraying every few days.

pests.name: Little leaf
pests.impact: Tiny leaves and no fruit; plants must be removed.

pests.name: Bacterial wilt
pests.impact: Sudden wilting in warm, wet soils.

postharvest.respiration: Non-climacteric; moderately sensitive to ethylene (calyx yellowing).
postharvest.chilling: Chilling injury below ~10 °C: pitting, browning of skin and seeds.
practices: Picked young and glossy every 3–5 days; over-mature fruit is seedy and fetches less.
Packed in gunny bags or crates (20–40 kg); mostly sold within 300 km.
Gloss and calyx freshness drive price; shading and quick sale matter more than cold chain.

steps.what: Frequent pickings; sorted by type and size.
Sold the same day at a nearby APMC or to a trader at the farm gate.
Vendors and quick commerce; strong regional preference by type.

supply_chain.packaging: Gunny bags and crates; rarely refrigerated.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

policy.what: Moratorium on commercial release of Bt brinjal (Bt brinjal is grown in Bangladesh since 2014).
DoCA tracks brinjal among its 38 essential commodities.

history.what: Monsoon pest and rain damage lift prices for a few weeks.
Winter glut: farm prices fall to a few rupees per kg.

signals: Arrivals in Kolkata, Hyderabad and Delhi mandis (Agmarknet).
Rainfall and cyclone tracks over Bengal and Odisha.
Borer and little-leaf advisories from state agriculture universities.
business: Regional and type-specific: what sells in Kolkata (round, light purple) differs from Hyderabad (small round) and Delhi (bharta).
Residue-tested and IPM brinjal (pheromone traps for the borer) is a premium niche for modern retail.
Short supply chains reward peri-urban sourcing and same-day delivery.
